questions.question: What should you do if suspension parts are broken?

options.text: Repair them, but it is not urgent.
You cannot tell if they are broken.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous and must be repaired immediately.

questions.question: When should you shift to a lower gear before going down a steep hill?

options.text: Before you start going down the hill.
After you have already started going down the hill.
As far down the hill as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start going down the hill.
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before you start going downhill. This prepares your vehicle for gravity, which will make it go faster on the downhill slope.

questions.question: What should you pay extra attention to during a winter pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: In winter, check coolant and antifreeze levels, heating equipment, windshield wipers, tires and chains, lights, windows and mirrors, handholds and steps, radiator shutters, and the exhaust system.

questions.question: What should you NOT do while driving a bus with passengers?

options.text: Refuel the bus while passengers are on board.

questions.explanation: Do not talk with passengers because it distracts you from driving. Never refuel with passengers on board. Do not tow or push a disabled bus with passengers aboard, unless it is unsafe for them to leave the bus.

questions.question: When do bridges usually freeze?

options.text: Only when temperatures are well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the roadway. Be extra careful on bridges when it is near freezing.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Increase the gap between your car and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the gap between your car and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead. This gives you more room to react and gives the tailgater room to pass. Do not speed up, because the tailgater may follow you at the higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: What happens to your vehicle when traveling downhill?

options.text: It travels at the same speed as on flat ground.

questions.explanation: Gravity makes your vehicle go faster when going downhill. Adjust your speed before you reach the downhill section.

questions.question: How much should you reduce your speed on packed snow?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on surfaces with poor grip. On packed snow, reduce your speed by one-half or more.

questions.question: How should you brake if your ABS is not working?

options.text: Brake normally. Your regular brakes still work.
Pump the brake pedal over and over.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally. Your regular brakes still work.
questions.explanation: Without a working ABS system, your vehicle still has normal brakes. Drive and brake as you normally would. Have your ABS fixed as soon as you can.

questions.question: What should you do before backing up in an unfamiliar area?

options.text: Get out and walk around the area to see what is there.
Do not use both side mirrors because it is distracting.
Wait for someone else to back up so you can see how they do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk around the area to see what is there.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out of your vehicle and look at the area. Check the sides and above for obstacles.

questions.question: While driving, you should monitor your gauges to:
questions.explanation: Check your gauges while driving for signs of trouble. Before you start driving, make sure all gauges are working correctly.

questions.question: Looking at your mirrors for too long is dangerous because:

options.text: You may not see what is happening ahead on the road.
The mirrors may shake and move.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not see what is happening ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: If you look at your mirrors too long, you may travel far without knowing what is ahead of you. Always be aware of everything around you.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT cause hydraulic brake failure?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure usually happens in two ways: loss of hydraulic pressure or overuse on long hills causing brake fade.

questions.question: When inspecting the inside of a bus, you should:
questions.explanation: When inspecting a bus interior, make sure everything is safe and working. Check that all handholds and railings are secure and safe to use.

questions.question: Emergency equipment in a vehicle is:

options.text: Only required when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Before you drive, check for emergency equipment: spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, six fuses, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Helps you stay awake on long trips.
Can damage the engine and transmission.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can damage the engine and transmission.
questions.explanation: Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle. Always accelerate slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: A ramp's posted speed limit:

options.text: May be too fast for large trucks and commercial vehicles.
Is just a suggestion and can be exceeded.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be too fast for large trucks and commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Ramp speed limits are set for cars. Large or heavily loaded trucks may need to go slower than the posted speed.

questions.question: If you have a drunk passenger on your bus, you should:

options.text: Make them exit the bus immediately.
Let them off at a safe place, like a scheduled stop or well-lit area.
Give them coffee to sober up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them off at a safe place, like a scheduled stop or well-lit area.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for a drunk passenger's safety. Have them exit in a safe location, such as a scheduled stop or a well-lit area with other people present.

questions.question: During a trip, gauges are:

options.text: The only way to know about vehicle problems.
One way to learn about vehicle problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: One way to learn about vehicle problems.
questions.explanation: During a trip, regularly check your gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights for problems.

questions.question: You are most likely to encounter strong winds when:
questions.explanation: Strong winds can push your vehicle out of its lane. This is especially dangerous when exiting a tunnel.
